newsitem.title: USA: CVRD delay could hurt Brazil - Morgan Stanley.
newsitem.headline: CVRD delay could hurt Brazil - Morgan Stanley.

text.p: Brazil's economy could be hurt if the repeatedly postponed sale of state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) is long delayed, an Morgan Stanley executive involved in the privatization said Monday.
Alex Seferian, a vice president of mergers and acquisitions, said he was confident the sale of CVRD would go through despite a flurry of court orders blocking it.

"It's a question of time in getting the legal issues resolved," said Seferian, part of Morgan Stanley's team advising a consortium headed by Anglo American Corp of South Africa and Brazil's Votorantim Inc.
"I'm generally optimistic about this legal battle that's taking place."
However, he added that a delay of more than a few weeks could start to raise doubts about Brazil's commitment to privatization and economic reforms.

Those concerns could lead to a drop in investors' interest in Brazil and the sale of its state companies. Brazil has planned for the multibillion-dollar sale of telephone and power companies starting late this year and in 1998.
"This would be sending a wrong signal to financial markets," he said.
"If this is delayed a few months, it could have a ripple effect on the entire economy" by raising questions about how well the reformist government can carry out its policies, he said.
"The minimal delays you can consider part of the process, but if it's going to be postponed months -- from anybody's perspective (that) is a negative."
CVRD is the world's biggest exporter of iron ore. Once completed, the privatization would be worth $5 billion, the biggest sale of a state company in Latin American history.

The government had scheduled the auction of CVRD, the crown jewel of state-owned companies, for April 29. However, it was delayed because opponents of the privatization got scores of court orders barring the sale.
A Brazilian judge is considering an appeal that would let all orders be judged by a single court, thus speeding the sale.
The judge could rule on the case by Tuesday.
